what_is_verified: The header contract: the published table's columns are Rank, Player, Team, Position, Value, in that order.
Value formatting: a dollar sign followed by an integer, e.g. '$74'. No decimals appear anywhere in the table.
Multi-position cells are comma-separated inside one cell, e.g. 'SF,PF'.
Player names are rendered 'First Last' with no suffix column.
The tail of the table carries an explicit '$0' rather than an empty cell, which is a published claim that a player is not worth rostering, not an absent price.
The page states: 'The prices are optimized for 8-category leagues with 156 rostered players'.
No budget, team count or per-team dollar figure is printed anywhere on the page.
what_is_synthetic: Every player name, team, position and dollar value in the CSV. FantraxHQ's table is editorial content and this repository redistributes none of it.
The row count. The published table has 194 rows; this fixture has 10, chosen to exercise the same branches (multi-position cell, explicit $0 tail, ignored Rank column).

transcription_of_the_published_table.note: Counted and summed by hand from the live page on 2026-08-21 in order to test the '$200 budget' inference that arrived with this source. The inference did not survive it.

the_inference_that_failed.claim_tested: FantraxHQ prices a standard 12-team, $200-per-team auction, so its basis can be inferred as $200.
the_inference_that_failed.rounding_noise_derivation: The published values are whole dollars, so each carries at most $0.50 of rounding, with standard deviation 1/sqrt(12) = 0.289. Over 156 independent roundings the sum's standard deviation is sqrt(156) * 0.289 = 3.6. A $255 gap is roughly seventy standard deviations away and is not rounding.
the_inference_that_failed.conclusion: basis_budget is UNESTABLISHED for this source, not $200. The published pool implies $221.25 per team at 12 teams, which is not a number any league uses, so the discrepancy is more likely to be in the method than in the team count.
the_inference_that_failed.what_survives: 156 rostered players is printed on the page, and 12 teams x 13 roster slots = 156 exactly. Team count and roster size remain reasonable INFERRED values with that arithmetic as the note. Only the budget is unestablished.

what_could_not_be_established: Whether a 2026-27 edition of this table exists. Only the 2025-26 page was read, so the header contract is what was verified, not the season.
The arithmetic behind the values. The article publishes no methodology, which is why the source's derivation_method is 'editorial' rather than a z-score family.
Which eight categories the '8-category' label refers to. The count is recorded in basis_category_count; the identity of the categories is not mechanically checkable and belongs in basis_note.
